findings.claim: In the four usable TEST DATA financial answers, two misinterpret NPV: one as an annual expense and one as savings. Two distinguish discounted project value from capital cost. This is a simulated coding observation, not a real-user rate.
Three of four TEST DATA carbon answers use avoided emissions or a scenario difference; one treats captured CO2 as avoided and expresses uncertainty.

Two of three answered change prompts request an NPV explanation; the third asks for no change. One of four friction answers identifies carbon boundaries instead of money, and one reports no difficulty.

payload.counterevidence: Two simulated financial answers are consistent with the model, one record reports no difficulty/no change, and another prioritizes capture versus avoidance. The proposed finance explanation is not unanimously needed.

unresolved.question: Would a short sign/time-boundary explanation enable a better handoff, or would carbon definitions remain the more consequential first change? Requests alone cannot resolve that choice.

limitations: All records are deterministic TEST DATA; there are no real participants or population estimates.
COMPLETE=6, retrieved=8 and usable=4 are different quantities; two duplicate copies, one malformed row and one preview were excluded. The change question has denominator 3, other questions 4.
Interpretation is Codex's qualitative coding of the validated fixture values, not a deterministic validator's research judgment or proof that a design will work.
